turns.text: real quick can u write an email to my stats tutoring coordinator. i got my stats grade up to a C+ and i wanna push it to a B so i need an extra slot every week on top of the one i have
Congrats on the C+, that's real progress. Happy to draft it. A few things so the email fits: what days/times can you actually do, and what's the coordinator's name?

dont know the name just put a placeholder. i have afternoon sections mon wed thu 2-5:15 so it has to be before 2. also im on ten hour nights sun thru thu so im wiped in the mornings and need to sleep. so like late morning/early afternoon at the earliest

Got it. So something in the early afternoon before your 2:00 sections, on days that work with your sleep. Here's a draft:

Subject: Request for an Additional Weekly Stats Tutoring Slot

Hi [coordinator's name],

I've been coming to the stats tutoring center and it's made a real difference. My grade has gone up to a C+ and I'd like to bring it up to a B by the end of the semester.

Could I add a second weekly session? I have afternoon classes Monday, Wednesday and Thursday from 2:00 to 5:15, so anything before 2:00 would work, ideally [your preferred days/times]. I'm also glad to take a cancellation or waitlist spot if that's easier.

Thanks for your time,
[your name]
[student ID, if they ask for it]

Want it shorter or less formal?
nah thats good. i also gotta catch up on biomech and ex phys this weekend off fatimas shared notes so stats is the one i wanna cover with the tutor. can u add that

Sure. Here's the line to add after the first paragraph:

"I'm keeping up with my other courses on my own using shared class notes, so stats is the one where I'd most like the extra support."

I left out the classmate's name since it's not needed, but you can add it if you like. Want a quick study plan for the new slot too?
lol ok that helped. short version of a plan pls, like what to do in the session

Short version:
1. Bring last week's quiz or homework and flag the problems you missed.
2. Redo those problems with the tutor, talking through each step.
3. Do 3-5 fresh practice problems on the same topic.
4. End by writing down what's coming up next so you can prep.

Do that weekly and a B is a realistic target.
